To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) video sharing sites have control over the reception quality and that (ii) only half of the video is downloaded and that this drops to 20% when the reception quality is poor.
the server side policy has a major impact on the viewing experience of the users, and that the reception quality is a major factor for the user to stop downloading a video.
YouTube and DailyMotion have a major control on the delivery of the videos and their reception quality, and that this control is used to improve the reception quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of network conditions on the video viewing experience, and how this impacts user behavior.
the evolution of HTTP video streaming traffic from the ISP perspective, and how it is impacted by the reception quality.
understanding the impact of the video sharing sites on the Internet traffic and the impact of video reception quality on the viewing behavior of the users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of experience of video streaming is highly dependent on the reception quality, and that the reception quality is controlled by the video sharing service provider.

the quality of experience for HTTP video streaming is highly dependent on the video sharing site, on the user's ISP, on the video itself, on the user viewing behavior, and on the network conditions between the user and the server.
video sharing sites are very much in control of the delivery of video to the user, and that this delivery is not always successful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the video sharing sites are able to adapt to the network conditions and the user’s behavior.
the reception quality of video streams is a crucial aspect that has to be taken into account when studying HTTP streaming traffic.
the video sharing sites are in control of the delivery of the videos to users and that this control is exercised through DNS resolution and the streaming policy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the video sharing site has the power to control the reception quality of its videos and the user behavior.
it shows the importance of understanding the impact of the video delivery infrastructure and the reception quality on the viewing behavior.

it shows that the reception quality of streaming videos is a major concern for the end-users, and that the video sharing sites are not doing enough to ensure the best possible reception quality for the end-users.
